_about: The Microsoft Store listing for Vesopa Express's first release (9N5W5VLP2948): the words, the properties and which picture goes where. The first submission had to be typed into Partner Center (see README, 'A new app's first submission'); this is what was typed, kept so the next person changing the listing starts from it. Every paragraph is one line: Partner Center shows each newline as a line break. The pictures are the Store's copies under Documents, not in this repository.

submission.notesForCertification:
Vesopa Express is a self-service ordering kiosk for venues that use the Vesopa EPOS till system. It works only for a venue that has switched Vesopa Express on in the Vesopa back office, and a kiosk is set up by a manager of that venue signing in once with their Vesopa account.

On first start the app shows its setup screen, "Set up this kiosk", with a "Continue with Vesopa" button and an "Exit Vesopa Express" button. The Exit button closes the app.

By design the app runs full screen, without a title bar, and ignores the close button and Alt+F4: it is a public kiosk that customers must not be able to close. Once a kiosk has been set up, staff leave it by holding the bottom-left corner of the screen for three seconds, entering the venue's passcode and choosing Exit in Settings.

The app never handles card details. Card payments are taken on a separate Dojo card machine, which the Vesopa server starts and checks; the app only shows the customer what the card machine is asking for.

internetClient is used to reach the Vesopa back office over HTTPS. privateNetworkClientServer is used to print tickets on a receipt printer on the venue's own network (port 9100).

listing.description:
Vesopa Express is a self-service ordering kiosk for your venue.

It is the kiosk for Vesopa EPOS. A customer walks up, touches the screen, orders from your menu, pays on the card machine beside it and takes a collection number. The order goes to the kitchen the moment it is paid, and your staff can get on with the food instead of taking orders at the counter.

REQUIRES A VESOPA EPOS ACCOUNT
This app is a companion to the Vesopa EPOS till system and cannot be used on its own. Vesopa Express is switched on for each venue in the Vesopa back office, and it stays off until you turn it on. Each kiosk is set up by a manager signing in once with their Vesopa account. Card payments need a Dojo card machine, paired with the kiosk in the back office.

YOUR MENU, NOT ANOTHER ONE
The kiosk shows the menu you already keep in the Vesopa back office for ordering at the table: the same sections, pictures, prices, add-ons and allergen information. Change a price in the back office and the kiosk changes with it. There is no second menu to keep up to date.

BUILT THE WAY PEOPLE ORDER
Touch to start, eat in or take away, then the menu, with its sections down the side and pictures big enough to see from a step back. Each dish opens with its choices and the price follows them as they are picked. "Make it a meal" takes the customer through the size, the side and the drink one step at a time, then shows the whole meal before it goes in the basket. Before paying, the basket suggests a few things that you choose, once, and takes "Not today, thanks" for an answer.

PAID MEANS PAID
The kiosk never holds a card or a payment key. The Vesopa server asks Dojo to take the payment on the card machine next to the screen, and the kiosk tells the customer what the machine wants: tap, insert or swipe, then approved. Only a completed payment becomes a sale, and it is recorded once, in the same reports as your till. A declined card can be tried again without starting the order over, and if the kiosk loses power while someone is paying, it picks the payment back up when it restarts.

A NUMBER TO COLLECT BY
Every paid order gets a collection number from a range you set, starting again each day. The number fills the screen, and the kiosk can print it on a ticket. A collection board for any TV or monitor shows the numbers moving from Preparing to Ready. It is a web page at a private address, so there is nothing to install on the screen.

STRAIGHT TO THE KITCHEN
Paid kiosk orders go to your Vesopa Kitchen screens, split by station exactly as the till would send them, with a meal's side and drink listed under the meal. The back office lists the day's kiosk orders, and staff can mark each one ready and then collected.

A TICKET FROM THE KIOSK'S OWN PRINTER
Connect a receipt printer to the kiosk by USB, through Windows, or on your network, and set it up in the kiosk's staff settings with a test ticket. The ticket carries your receipt branding, the collection number, what was ordered, the total with VAT and how it was paid. You choose in the back office whether it prints every time, only when the customer asks, or never.

LOCKED TO THE JOB
The kiosk runs full screen, with no title bar and nothing a customer can close or minimise. The only way out is the staff settings, opened from a hidden corner and protected by a passcode you choose when the kiosk is set up. The passcode is checked on the kiosk itself, so staff can still get in when the internet is down. Add Windows assigned access and the kiosk stays on your menu all day.

FOR EVERY CUSTOMER
Every screen adapts to portrait or landscape and to the size of the display, from a floor-standing kiosk to a countertop tablet. Lower the screen brings the menu within reach of a wheelchair user or a child, and high contrast makes every screen easier to read. If a customer walks away, "Still there?" counts down before the basket is cleared, so the next person starts afresh.

YOURS TO SET UP
In the Vesopa back office, under Dine-in & QR, you switch Vesopa Express on, offer eat in, take away or both, choose whether to ask for the customer's name, set the welcome message and picture, set the collection number range and how long the kiosk waits before asking "Still there?", pick the suggestions, set up meals, pair each kiosk with its card machine and see the day's orders.

Runs on Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) and Windows 11, on a touchscreen.

listing.releaseNotes:
Version 1.0.0.0 - The first release of Vesopa Express

Vesopa Express is the self-service ordering kiosk for Vesopa EPOS. Customers order from your own menu, make it a meal, pay on the Dojo card machine beside the screen and take a collection number.

Only a completed payment becomes a sale. It is recorded once, in the same reports as your till, sent to your Vesopa Kitchen screens by station, and shown on the collection board until it is collected.

Switch it on for your venue in the Vesopa back office under Dine-in & QR, then set each kiosk up by signing in with your Vesopa account.
